transcript.content: Hello, it's good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well, I came in because my head just feels foggy lately. I keep mixing up simple things—appointment times, dates for exhibits, and even which volunteer I already called. It’s frustrating, and it’s not like me.
Have you been forgetting recent conversations?

Yes, I think so—at least parts of them. I’ll talk to someone and then later I’m not sure if I already called them or what we settled on. It’s the same kind of fogginess, mixing up appointments or exhibit dates. It’s frustrating.
Does this feel like a real change from how your memory used to be?

Yes, it does. I used to be pretty clear about those things, but lately my head feels foggy. I keep mixing up simple things—appointment times, exhibit dates, who I already called—and that’s not how I usually am.
Have these memory problems started to interfere with your daily activities?

Yes, it has. I’ve missed doctor visits because I got the times mixed up, and I’ve messed up the senior center schedule more than once. My husband has had to step in and help me with calls and calendars… even decisions about repairs that I used to handle on my own. It’s upsetting, honestly.
Do you ever get confused about what day or month it is?
I don’t know if I’d say the day or month exactly, but my head does feel foggy. I keep mixing up simple things, like appointment times, exhibit dates, and which volunteer I already called.
Did these memory problems begin after any illness, injury, or new medication?
I’m not really sure. I can’t think of a particular illness or injury that started it, and I don’t know about a new medicine causing it. It just sort of became noticeable over time.
Have you been feeling down or depressed most days lately?
I’m not really sure. I’ve been upset and frustrated about the memory trouble, but I don’t know that I’d say I feel depressed most days.
Have you gotten lost in places that should be familiar to you?
No, I don’t think I’ve gotten lost in familiar places. Not that I can remember. I might get turned around for a minute, but I usually know where I am.
Have you been feeling excessively worried or anxious lately?
I don’t think so. I mean, I get worried about things now and then, especially when I forget something, but I wouldn’t say I’ve been excessively anxious lately.
Have these memory problems been gradually getting worse over time?
Yes, I think so. It’s more that my head feels foggy, and I keep mixing up simple things—like appointment times, exhibit dates, or which volunteer I already called. That’s really what brought me in.
Have you been hearing or seeing things that other people don’t seem to?
No, I haven’t noticed anything like that. I don’t hear voices or see things other people don’t, as far as I know.
Have you been diagnosed with any medical or neurological condition that affects your brain or memory?
Not that I know of. I haven’t been told I have any brain or nerve condition. I’m here because of the memory trouble, but I don’t have a diagnosis for it.
Are you still able to manage your finances on your own?

I’m not really doing it all on my own anymore. My husband’s had to step in more—helping with calls and keeping the calendar straight. I’ve missed some doctor visits, and I’ve gotten the senior center schedule mixed up badly. He’s also helping with decisions about repairs, things I used to handle myself.
Have you ever had a stroke?
Not that I’m aware of. No one has ever told me I had a stroke.
Have you been diagnosed with Alzheimer’s disease?
No, I haven’t been diagnosed with Alzheimer’s disease, not that anyone has told me.
Have you ever been told you have Parkinson’s disease?
No, I don’t think so. I’ve never been told I have Parkinson’s disease.
Has any doctor ever told you that your memory problems are due to another medical condition?
No, I don’t think any doctor has told me it was from some other medical condition. At least, not that I remember.
Has a doctor ever told you that you have a medical condition that could be causing these memory problems?
Not that I know of. No doctor has told me I have some medical condition causing memory problems.
Have you had any memory testing done by a doctor, and were you told it showed a problem?
I’m not sure. I don’t remember having any special memory test with a doctor, and I don’t recall anyone telling me it showed a problem.
Have you ever been told you have a medical illness that affects your brain?
Not that I’m aware of. I don’t think anyone’s told me I have an illness affecting my brain.
